rationale: Three layers, one rule: keep what cannot be recreated, regenerate what can. The raw downloads and the uniform per-country files are irreplaceable and currently have no durability at all — they live outside any git repository, unhashed and unbacked. The per-municipality fan-out and the generated pages are build output: reproducible from the uniform layer, so they are regenerated into the serving snapshot rather than committed. The manifest this config produces stays in git, which is what keeps the whole chain auditable after the fan-out stops being committed.

layers.title: Original downloads, exactly as fetched
layers.recreatable: only by refetching national sources, several of which are not stable: Costa Rica is a portal query, Spain publishes year-stamped archives that are replaced in place

layers.title: One normalised file per country
layers.recreatable: from raw, by rerunning the country extractors

layers.title: Per-municipality fan-out
layers.recreatable: directly from uniform; verified identical — 28,559 entities and 4,120,493 detail rows, no field present here that is absent upstream
layers.note: Regenerated into the public serving snapshot each release. prepare-public-serving-snapshots.mjs already treats this directory as a snapshot input.

layers.title: Generated municipal profile pages
layers.recreatable: from the uniform layer via scripts/build-municipal-expansion-pages.py and scripts/build-municipality-country-pages.mjs; run-to-run output verified byte-identical
layers.note: 29,597 files. Every regeneration rewrote all of them into history. Prerendered HTML is correct for SEO and no-JS readers; committing it is what was wrong.

layers.title: Generated Czech municipal pages
layers.recreatable: from pipeline/transforms/build_czech_site.py, the single source of every page under cz/

layers.title: Per-entity machine-readable profiles
layers.recreatable: from pipeline/transforms/build_municipal_public_site.py, which rebuilds the directory from scratch; verified byte-identical across 6,267 files. Inputs are data/municipal-snapshot.v1.json, data/benchmark.v1.json and data/large-city-history.v1.json, all committed.
layers.note: 6,254 municipalities are a verbatim fan-out of municipal-snapshot — every field reproduces from it exactly — plus the 13 Czech regions, which come from benchmark.v1.json.

layers.title: Municipal entity directory
layers.recreatable: from the serving fan-out today; from the warehouse plus each national source's own name column once the snapshot generator is rewired
layers.note: Entity identity extracted from the fan-out: name, region, population, currency, reporting basis and page URL for 28,559 municipalities across 15 countries, 4.6 MB against the fan-out's 580 MB. This is the layer whose absence kept the fan-out alive. The warehouse holds every fact those files carry — verified for BR:1100015, where actual/TotalReceitas reproduces the published 147,350,577.63 to the cent — but it does not know that CR:SIPP-ABANGARES is Abangares. Small enough to commit, so it is committed.

known_gaps.detail: Denmark has no subtree under data/source_cache/municipal-expansion. Its uniform file exists and Denmark is also loaded in BigQuery, so the data is not at risk, but the raw provenance chain is incomplete for that country.

The committed pages are stale relative to their template: regenerating applies the copy-voice rewrite they never received, and a sort-order and numeric-type normalisation in international-municipalities.v1.json. Refreshing that baseline is a separate reviewable change from un-committing, and is deliberately not bundled here.

Brazil's extractor mislabels budget_side on 454,916 rows. 101 revenue codes — ReceitaTributaria, Impostos, Taxas, TransferenciasCorrentes among them — arrive marked `expenditure` across all 5,570 municipalities, and none ever arrives marked `revenue`. The RREO column heading is authoritative (revenue uses PREVISÃO / No Bimestre / Até o Bimestre; expenditure uses DOTAÇÃO / DESPESAS), so the warehouse loader corrects from it and flags each corrected row side_corrected_from_source_column. The uniform layer and the committed per-municipality files still carry the defect, so the live site shows it until the extractor is fixed upstream or the fan-out is regenerated from a corrected view. Detectable only because Brazil publishes column labels; the other countries carry none, though their revenue-to-expenditure balances are all plausible.

Japan is analysed but not loaded. Its side rules, stock exclusions (outstanding local-bond debt, fund balances), headcount exclusions and financing classification are settled in scripts/load-municipal-facts-jpn.py, but the main budget tables carry a parent-child hierarchy the uniform layer does not express: table 4 lists a parent tax category beside its own child with no marker, and tables 7-13 pair a 総額 total with the components it totals plus an うち (of which) column that is a subset of its neighbour. Leaf sums therefore come to 2.47x a municipality's published headline revenue and 0.50x its expenditure. The script refuses to write rather than publish that. The e-Stat table definitions state each row's parent and would turn is_summary_row from a guess into a lookup.

The fan-out is stale where the warehouse is corrected. For BR:1100015 only 69 of 239 fan-out detail rows survive as-is: the files predate the budget_side repair and carry a different stage vocabulary (`cash`, `execution`) than the loaded lifecycle (`enacted → revised → committed → actual → paid`). The headline reconciles exactly, so the published figures are not at risk, but the two are not interchangeable and the fan-out is the wrong one. Retiring it needs prepare-public-serving-snapshots.mjs to build profiles from the warehouse and the entity directory rather than from these files.

Japan is the only country whose facts the warehouse cannot supply, so data/municipal-expansion/jpn (110.9 MB, 1,741 entities) must stay until the e-Stat hierarchy is settled. Its identity is already extracted, so the other fourteen countries are no longer waiting on it.

Twelve of the fourteen warehouse countries reproduce their published headline exactly from warehouse rows (pipeline/config/municipal_headline_rules.json). Three things had to be modelled before that held. The grain includes fiscal_period: Brazil's RREO reports the same stage twice, once for the bimester and once cumulative, and summing both reports a year as roughly double itself. The rule varies by year: a closed year publishes its outturn and a forthcoming one its appropriation, so Spain and Georgia each split almost exactly in half between `actual` and `enacted` — which read as a half-broken rule rather than two correct ones. And where item codes are nested numerically, as Spain's chapter/article/concept are, every level restates the one above, so the headline is one depth rather than a sum of rows; the warehouse does not mark those as summary rows, so depth is read off the code.

Brazil's published expenditure is the one headline the warehouse cannot supply: only 4 of 40 sampled municipalities have that value anywhere in their facts, at any stage or period, while revenue reproduces on 39 of 39. So it is not a rule waiting to be found — the figure was computed from something not loaded. Brazil's revenue rule is actual@FY / ReceitasExcetoIntraOrcamentarias, matching the importer's own choice of the 'Até o Bimestre' column.

Denmark publishes no headline at all today — its profiles carry a history row with a year and a stage and no amounts — so there is no baseline a regeneration could regress, only one it could add. Two things to settle first: the warehouse carries the Danish source's sign convention unchanged, so revenue arrives negative (Copenhagen 2025: revenue -68.82bn DKK, expenditure 35.75bn), and that expenditure looks low for a municipality whose budget is nearer 50-60bn, which suggests the expenditure side is not yet complete rather than merely unsigned.
